title: Automated Bisect
description: Automate git bisect with run commands and scripts to find regressions without manual testing.

data.text: git bisect supports automation through the run subcommand and the BISECT_RUN environment variable. Instead of manually testing each commit, you provide a script or command that returns 0 (good), 1 (bad), or 125 (skip). Git runs it at each bisect step automatically.

git bisect run <command> executes the command at each bisect step. The command should be a script, test, or any program that exits 0 if the bug is not present and 1 if it is. Exit code 125 tells Git to skip that commit.

data.title: Automated bisect with a test script
data.code:
# Step 1: Create a test script
cat > bisect-test.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Run a specific test that reproduces the bug
npm test -- --grep "User login validation"

# Exit 0 = good (no bug)
# Exit 1 = bad (bug present)
EOF

chmod +x bisect-test.sh

# Step 2: Start bisect with run
git bisect start
git bisect bad HEAD
git bisect good v2.1.0

# Step 3: Let Git run the test automatically
git bisect run ./bisect-test.sh

# Git reports:
# abc1234 is the first bad commit

data.title: Exit 125 aborts the bisect if used incorrectly
data.text: Only return 125 when a commit genuinely cannot be tested (e.g., the build fails for unrelated reasons). Returning 125 for every commit will cause bisect to abort.
For simple checks, you can pass an inline command to bisect run without creating a separate script file.

data.title: Bisect run with inline command
data.code:
# Check if a file contains a specific string
git bisect start
git bisect bad HEAD
git bisect good v2.1.0

git bisect run bash -c '
  if grep -q "ERROR: token validation failed" src/auth/*.cs; then
    exit 1  # bad
  else
    exit 0  # good
  fi
'

# Git identifies the commit that introduced the error string

data.text: When the regression is a build failure rather than a runtime bug, your bisect script can check whether the project builds successfully at each commit.

data.title: Bisect for build regressions
data.code:
cat > bisect-build.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Try to build the project
npm run build > /dev/null 2>&1
BUILD_EXIT=$?

if [ $BUILD_EXIT -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "Build succeeded"
  exit 0  # good
else
  echo "Build failed"
  exit 1  # bad
fi
EOF

chmod +x bisect-build.sh

git bisect start
git bisect bad HEAD
git bisect good v2.0.0
git bisect run ./bisect-build.sh

items.question: What if the build is broken at both good and bad commits?
items.answer: You cannot bisect when the good commit is also broken. Find a known-good commit where the build passes and the bug is absent.

items.question: Can bisect run run tests in parallel?
items.answer: You can write a script that runs tests in parallel, but bisect itself runs sequentially — one commit at a time.

items.question: Can I use CI builds with bisect?
items.answer: Not directly — bisect checks out commits locally. However, you can use git bisect run to trigger a local build or a subset of tests.

items.question: What if my bisect script is slow?
items.answer: Optimize the script to run only the specific check needed. Use targeted tests (--grep), cached builds, and incremental test runners.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: git bisect run automates the entire bisect process with a script or command
Exit 0 = good, exit 1 = bad, exit 125 = skip
Use targeted tests or checks that run in seconds, not minutes
For build regressions, check npm run build or dotnet build at each step
bisect run can use inline commands or external scripts
